newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North sees lower U.S. iron ore sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North sees lower U.S. iron ore sales.

text.p: Mining house North Ltd managing director Campbell Anderson sid on Thursday the company expected U.S. sales for its Robe River iron ore operation would fall in the current year and that South Korean sales would remain steady.

"We anticipate further fluctuations in sales to each of the businesses markets in the near future with Japan expected to improve as its steel sector recovers, but U.S. sales are likely to decrease following stock reduction at Robe's major customer, Bethlehem Steel," Anderson told the company's annual meeting.
"South Korean sales are expected to remain steady and Robe will continue to explore market opportunities in China and the surrounding region," he said.
Anderson also said that North continued to evaluate the Marramamba iron ore deposit at West Angelas in Western Australia for potential lump and sinter fines iron ore production.
"Pending further investigation of a possible West Angelas development we decided to defer any restart of the pellet plant operation at Robe," he said.
Robe River, also located in Western Australia, contributed A$109.4 million to North's group earnings in 1995/96, down 8.6 percent on the previous year, despite a production increase of 6.5 percent.
